title: Geometry - Lesson 2 Practice: Quadrilateral Classification
description: Practice classifying quadrilaterals by definition, hierarchy, and given properties instead of appearance.

questions.question: Which definition describes a parallelogram?
options: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides
A quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel opposite sides
A quadrilateral with four right angles only
A quadrilateral with two pairs of adjacent congruent sides
questions.explanation: A parallelogram is defined by two pairs of parallel opposite sides.

questions.question: A quadrilateral has four right angles, but no side lengths are marked congruent. What classification is guaranteed?
questions.explanation: Four right angles guarantee a rectangle. It could be a square, but that is not guaranteed without equal side lengths.

questions.question: Every square is also a rectangle.
questions.explanation: A square has four right angles, so it satisfies the definition of rectangle.

questions.question: Every rectangle is also a square.
questions.explanation: A rectangle does not have to have four congruent sides, so it is not always a square.

questions.question: A quadrilateral with two distinct pairs of adjacent congruent sides is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A kite has two distinct pairs of adjacent congruent sides.

questions.question: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is the most specific classification?
questions.explanation: Exactly one pair of parallel sides describes a non-parallelogram trapezoid.

questions.question: Explain why a square can be classified as both a rectangle and a rhombus.
questions.correctAnswer: A square has four right angles, so it is a rectangle, and it has four congruent sides, so it is a rhombus.
questions.explanation: Classification is based on definitions. A square satisfies both the rectangle and rhombus definitions.

questions.question: A diagram looks like a rhombus, but no side lengths or congruence marks are given. Why should you not classify it as a rhombus yet?
questions.correctAnswer: Appearance is not enough evidence. A rhombus must have four congruent sides, so the diagram needs side marks, measurements, or a given statement.
questions.explanation: Formal classification depends on guaranteed properties, not how the figure looks.
